questions.q: Why is a three-step agent loop necessarily at least three times slower than a single well-crafted prompt?
options: Because agents always use a slower, less capable model
Because each loop iteration (Lesson 2) is a full model round trip, so more steps directly means more round trips
Because tool definitions are illegal to send more than once
Speed has nothing to do with the number of loop iterations
questions.explain: Every plan/act/observe iteration from Lesson 2 requires its own model call, so latency compounds directly with step count.

questions.q: What is the simple test this lesson proposes for whether a task needs a real agent loop?
options: Whether the task description is longer than one sentence
Whether the user is a paying customer
Whether it would be fun to build with an agent
Whether answering well requires information discovered through more than one step, where later steps depend on earlier results
questions.explain: If a task doesn't need multi-step, interdependent discovery, a single prompt (or at most a fixed workflow) is enough — no real agent loop is needed.

questions.q: In this lesson's terms, what is a 'workflow' as distinct from a true agent?
options: A workflow is just another name for a single chat prompt with no tools
A workflow requires more tool calls than an agent, not fewer
A workflow is code that calls the model and tools in a fixed, predetermined sequence, rather than letting the model decide the path step by step
A workflow and an agent are exactly the same thing with different names
questions.explain: When the sequence of steps never varies, your code can hard-code the path and still get tool access — without paying for the model to re-decide the obvious next step every time.

questions.q: Why does this lesson classify 'classify this support ticket into one of five categories' as agent-overkill?
options: Because classification tasks are impossible for language models
Because classification requires at least ten different tools
Because support tickets can never be read by a language model
Because it's a single, well-defined transformation a direct prompt already solves reliably, with no multi-step discovery needed
questions.explain: It's one pass from input to output with no dependency on information discovered mid-task — exactly the kind of task a loop adds cost and latency to for no benefit.

questions.q: What does Anthropic's own published guidance say about choosing between a simple prompt, a workflow, and an agent?
options: Always default to the most complex, fully agentic option available
Agents should never be used under any circumstances
Find the simplest solution possible, and only increase complexity when a simpler approach genuinely falls short
Workflows and agents are banned in production systems
questions.explain: The guidance is to start simple — often a single well-optimized LLM call is already enough — and reach for a workflow or full agent only when the task actually demands it.
